text.p: Property developer Del Webb Corp said on Thursday it was on track to post earnings of between $2.10 and $2.20 per share for fiscal 1997 but that it would be difficult to maintain record earnings.

"As we look forward to fiscal 1998, it will be difficult to maintain our earnings at this record level, primarily because of the build-out of Terravita, a lower backlog at the beginning of fiscal 1998 and the fact that we will not be adding any new Sun City communities during the year," Chairman Phil Dion said.
Terravita is a recreation-oriented community in north Scottsdale, Arizona.

Earlier in April, chief financial officer John Spencer gave analysts a similar outlook, saying that going into fiscal 1998, the company anticipated higher interest rates, a lack of new developments and a lower backlog would affect results.
Dion also said the company would set a record for closings in fiscal 1997 and it was investigating several new regions of the country as possible sites for new Sun City communities.
